_readme: TopCoat HQ Dashboard feature manifest. One entry per shipped feature: plain-English description (catalog quality) plus code anchors. Consult before grepping index.html. Anchors are FUNCTION NAMES, never line numbers. Update the relevant entry when shipping changes to a feature (CLAUDE.md rule 9). Generated 2026-07-18.

features.name: In-house estimator PWA
features.description: A mobile, installable estimating app that reps use in the driveway to price coating jobs from square footage and system type using the same catalog and margin math as job costing. It works fully offline (service worker plus local cache with a sync outbox) so an estimate built with no signal saves and uploads once the phone reconnects. Prompt 47: a new estimate defaults its salesperson to the LOGGED-IN rep, mapped explicitly by pec_sales_team_members.auth_user_id (set per member in Settings > Sales Team via openSalesTeamModal's Login picker; migration 2026-07-22_sales_member_auth_user.sql). An unmapped login gets a blank salesperson plus a get-mapped prompt, never a silent first-in-list fallback. Prompt 55 NARROWS prompt 47: once a salesperson is set, the select is read-only text for non-admins (admin check = admin_users.role threaded from App.tsx, FAIL CLOSED); the blank/unmapped case stays editable for everyone so the get-mapped path never dead-ends. Shared rules (draft gate, trigger, default priority) live in production/estimate-draft.cjs, fixture-tested.

features.name: Numbered estimate records
features.description: Every saved estimate becomes a sequential, searchable record (EST-102026 and up) with its own page showing customer info, price and margin, line items, optional add-ons, flake color, and the comps and AI price read behind the number. A dedicated Estimates list holds them all, and estimates can be archived and restored as a soft delete. Prompt 38: estimates can now be TEXTED as well as emailed. The same split Send control as invoices (default both channels); the text goes through pec-send-sms kind='estimate' (server-built body with the /e/<token> review-and-sign link + STOP line, lead/customer opt-out enforced, logged to pec_sms_log kind 'estimate' so it stays out of Last-invoiced), and a text-only send runs the same markEstimateSent flip + estimateSentLeadEffects as email so the estimate goes live either way. The blank-scope warn gate fires on any channel. Prompt 47 (card first): the estimate ROW now exists the moment the rep makes their first real edit in the estimator, written by an early draft save (parent row only, requires name/phone/email/address/salesperson, all prefilled in the lead flow) under the same pre-minted id the full Save upserts. Draft-status estimates show an 'In Draft' badge on the list rows and the detail header (the shared EST_STATUS_META draft label; numbering stays the Postgres sequence, so an unnumbered card reads '(unnumbered)' until its first sync).

features.name: Customer-facing estimate (send, sign, accept)
features.description: Reps send a private link where the customer reviews the scope and line items, ticks optional add-ons with a live-updating total, and accepts by typing their name to sign, or requests changes or declines with a reason. Accepting automatically creates the job on both the Jobs page and the Job Schedule with all areas and work-order details carried over, including a custom estimate's typed square footage (into the job's sqft) and the internal crew notes. A Preview button shows the exact customer page before sending.

features.name: Estimate view tracking
features.description: Every customer open of the public estimate page is logged (link-preview bots from SMS/email apps filtered by user agent) and, when enabled, drops a shared bell notification for all staff; clicking it opens the estimate. The estimate card's Customer view section shows Viewed N times with the last open time. Settings > Estimates carries the notification switch (default on) and an optional first-view-per-day throttle (default off).

features.name: Estimator duplicate-customer search
features.description: A search box on the estimator's customer card finds existing customers and leads by name, phone, email, or address as the rep types, labeling each result Customer or Lead with phone and address. Picking a match prefills the form and links the estimate through estimates.lead_id (a customer match reuses or creates its lead via leads.customer_id), so no duplicate record is created. Online-only; offline the search hides and the outbox save path is unchanged. Toggle in Settings > Estimates (estimator_customer_search_enabled).

features.name: Auto-written scope of work
features.description: Estimates assemble a polished, customer-facing scope of work from the company's real templates, filling in square footage, areas, and inclusions from the estimate itself while never altering exclusions or cure-time language. The estimator prompts reps to fill any template blanks on site, warns before a blank reaches the customer, and the AI writes the final version once, then only rewrites on an explicit Regenerate so hand edits are preserved.

features.name: Multi-system estimates
features.description: One estimate can cover several areas that each carry their own system (a flake garage plus a quartz patio), priced with each area's own recipe and rolled into a single price. The gross-profit target is the square-foot-weighted average of the systems in play so a small high-margin area does not skew the whole number.

features.name: Add-ons catalog
features.description: Reps drop upsells like stem walls, joint filling, upgrades, or drive time onto an estimate from a managed catalog, each with a prefilled price, real cost, unit, and scope paragraph. Because every add-on carries a cost, gross profit stays honest, and items marked optional stay out of the base total until the customer selects them.

features.name: Estimate pricing engine and controls
features.description: Estimates price from just the system and square footage using recipe default products and a per-system target gross profit, then show the full work behind the number: price per square foot, the cost stack (materials, labor, sundries, add-ons, commission, gross profit), and a plain-English explanation including charm rounding. Reps can override the sell price with a required reason and a floor confirmation, every estimate bakes in an adjustable 2% sundries cost, and moisture vapor barrier is chosen per area.

features.name: Custom estimate mode
features.description: A Standard/Custom switch lets reps price one-off work that does not fit the material calculator by typing the scope and price themselves, with add-ons still available. An optional Polish with AI button cleans up the typed scope wording without changing meaning, exclusions, or dollar figures, and can be undone. An optional square footage field shows a live read-only price per sqft (the price stays the typed number) and carries to the job's sqft on accept, lighting up the $/sqft readouts on Job Costing and the work order.

features.name: Crew notes on the work order
features.description: A short internal brief for the install crew (cliff notes on what the job is, plus watch-outs like access, prep, and site conditions), separate from the customer scope. Typed on the estimator in either mode or AI-drafted from the proposal with a manual Generate from proposal button (undoable, edits always win, never invents facts not in the estimate). It carries to the job on accept, stays editable on the job page's Job Card block, and prints in its own Crew Notes section on the crew work order. Strictly internal: it never appears on the customer proposal, estimate page, portal, or PDF. Prompt 55: the work order's Job Identity grid carries a Salesperson pair (fills the grid's former empty slot, so row count and the prompt-53 header height math are untouched); blank prints Unassigned, deliberately unlike the handwritten CREW/DATE hero boxes.

features.name: Live proposal panel
features.description: The customer-facing proposal builds live inside the estimator as reps work, drafting from scope templates the moment an area has a system and square footage. The AI writes the polished version automatically on the first save once scope questions are answered, then only rewrites on an explicit Regenerate, and reps can edit the text in place before sending.

features.name: Structured customer and address fields
features.description: The estimator's customer card starts with a Residential or Commercial choice, capturing first/last name or company name plus optional contact, and splits the address into real fields. With a Google key configured, typing a street suggests real addresses and fills city, state, and zip, while everything stays hand-editable and fully offline. Commercial estimates carry the company name onto the proposal and the customer record.

features.name: Leads pipeline board
features.description: A Kanban Leads board shows every lead as a card across six pre-sale stages from New to Accepted or Lost, with drag-to-advance, per-column counts and pipeline value, source/campaign/owner filters, and speed-to-lead timers that turn red after an hour so no lead sits unclaimed. Each card carries a Contacted Nx chip derived read-only from the outbound comms logs plus drip sends (calls, texts, emails matched by customer_id then normalized phone; drip ledger rows attributed by lead_id, with the drip mirror rows in the comms logs excluded so nothing double-counts; 0 reads Not contacted, red on an aging new lead) and a Hot/Warm/Cold AI score badge (70/40 cutoffs) with a hot-first sort in the filter bar. Facebook and Google form leads land in HQ automatically with an instant AI summary, 1-100 score, and next step, and duplicate submissions fold into the existing lead. Cards with an active drip enrollment show a small Drip chip.

features.name: Lead drip engine
features.description: Automatic AI-tailored follow-up drips for leads: new leads auto-enroll (intake webhook and manual add) in a seeded 30-day 8-step taper (days 1,2,4,7,11,16,22,30, SMS/email/both per step). A scheduled runner (every 15 min) re-checks four kill-switches at send time (lead replied via inbound text/call, stage advanced past contacted or lost, opted out, max touches), defers SMS outside 8am-8pm Phoenix, renders each message per lead with Claude (no invented facts, no em dashes, no links; scrubber enforces), and sends through the same Quo/Resend request shapes as the manual senders, mirroring rows into pec_sms_log (kind drip) / pec_email_log (template_key drip). Safety: global master switch (settings key drip_sending_enabled, ships OFF), per-campaign dry_run mode (default; writes review copy, never sends), claim-first concurrency (no double-send possible), first SMS carries Reply STOP to opt out, Quo STOP flips leads.opted_out and stops the enrollment. Admin Drips view (master switch, mode/pause toggles, steps, recent activity); lead detail shows a Drip card with Stop/Enroll and the messages in the timeline. Phase 3 generalized the engine to SUBJECTS: enrollments carry subject_type (lead or job) plus subject_id, one active enrollment per subject per campaign (a lead can hold a lead-nurture drip and an estimate drip at once, never two of the same), a recipient resolver maps a subject to its contact + consent model (lead = positive sms_consent; job = the customer's opt-out-only sms_opt_out), and kill-switches run a universal core plus a per-kind adapter. See the Estimate follow-up drip and Invoice payment reminders entries for the two Phase 3 kinds. Prompt 42 (go-live prep) added a GLOBAL approval gate: while the settings key drip_approval_required is 'true', a due step on a LIVE campaign renders its real copy into a 'pending' pec_drip_sends row (one per sendable leg, held once per step by a partial unique index) and the enrollment does NOT advance until a human approves, edits, or skips it in the Drip Approvals view; approving re-runs consent + kill-switches + quiet hours at that moment (a reply/STOP/payment/lost between render and approve voids the item with the reason shown), sends through the same providers, and advances with the same claim. SMS approved outside the window sits as 'queued' and is flushed by the runner at the window open with a final consent re-check. Quiet hours are settings-driven (drip_quiet_start/end/days, default 08:00-20:00 Phoenix Mon-Sat) and editable in Settings > Drips along with the master switch and the gate.

features.name: Estimate follow-up drip
features.description: When an estimate is sent to the customer, the lead automatically moves from the lead-nurture drip to an estimate follow-up drip (the nurture drip stops with reason estimate_sent so nobody is on two tracks). Taper: days 1, 3, 7, 14 after the send, AI-written warm nudges to review and sign. The message may state the estimate price only when the record carries one, and the real signing link (/e/token) is appended by code after the AI scrub, so the model can never invent a link or amount. Stops at send time when any of the lead's estimates is accepted or signed (the interim signed state counts), when all are rejected or the lead is lost, on a portal change request (counts as replied, a human takes over), on an inbound text or call, on opt-out, or at max touches. Re-sending a revised estimate after a stop starts a fresh taper. Runs on the shared drip engine (master switch + dry_run rules apply); campaign ships dry_run.

features.name: Invoice payment reminders
features.description: Automatic payment reminders for open invoices. The first time an invoice goes to the customer (email compose or the Text invoice button; both stamp jobs.invoice_first_sent_at first-send-wins) the JOB enrolls in a reminder drip: day 0, then +3, +7, +14 (no due-date column exists, so the send moment is the anchor). Every run the engine recomputes the real balance from jobs.price minus pec_payments; a partial payment keeps the reminders coming showing the remaining balance, and the payment that clears it stops the enrollment with reason paid on the next tick. The recipient is the job's customer; their STOP (sms_opt_out) silences the SMS leg while email reminders continue, and an inbound text or call stops the whole drip as replied. Balance and pay link (/pay/token) are appended by code, never written by the model. Voided or archived jobs stop as job_closed. Money guardrail: the campaign ships dry_run and stays there until Dylan reviews generated copy and flips it live himself. Prompt 45: when the job has a payment schedule, reminders state the current outstanding ask (deposit or installment, with its label) instead of the full balance, and stop as not_due while nothing is currently due.

features.name: Manual blast tool
features.description: One composed message to a filtered audience, sent from the Drips page via a 3-step wizard: compose (one shared SMS and/or email; {first_name} is the only personalization; an optional Draft with AI button drafts from a typed goal and can never invent offers the goal does not state), audience (filter leads by stage/source/campaign/brand and customers by tag/company, then deselect anyone; opt-outs and missing consent are hard-filtered BEFORE the count is shown with removed counts displayed, and recipients are de-duped by phone/email with leads winning collisions), and a confirm step stating the EXACT per-channel counts that nothing sends without. Recipients are materialized as queued rows in the shared pec_drip_sends ledger (blast_id set); the drain claims each row conditionally (queued -> sending -> sent/failed), re-checks consent at send time so a late STOP wins, holds SMS outside 8am-8pm Phoenix, and is resumable and double-send-proof by construction. pec-blast-run kicks immediate sending after confirm; the 15-minute drip tick is the safety net. The master switch gates blasts too. Every text carries Reply STOP to opt out; lead-directed blast sends count as outbound touches via the shared ledger.

features.name: Drip and blast performance metrics
features.description: Two Sales-section Metrics cards (the former Phase 3 placeholder slot). Drip performance: one row per sequence kind (lead nurture, estimate follow-up, invoice reminders) with its dry-run/LIVE chip, active enrollments right now, sends and dry-run previews in the window, replies, and conversions (stage advanced / signed / paid) with a conversion rate over enrollments that ended in the window, plus a stop-reason bar chart and a drill to the window's sends. Blast performance: recent blasts with sent/failed/skipped, opt-outs generated after confirm, per-blast drills, and a weekly sent-volume chart; notes honestly that blast replies are not machine-attributed. Both filter by the existing Metrics time window, degrade to a not-migrated notice pre-migration, and show honest empty states while data is thin.

features.name: Drip approval gate and settings controls
features.description: The supervised-launch layer over the drip engine (prompt 42). Drip Approvals (admin nav) lists every held drip message across leads and jobs, newest first: recipient with masked phone/email, campaign + step, and the editable body (plus subject for email). Per item: Approve & Send (re-checks consent, opt-out, replies, stage/paid/lost, and quiet hours at that exact moment, then sends via the normal providers, logs 'sent', and advances the enrollment exactly like an auto-send), Skip this step (advances without sending), Stop drip (ends the enrollment). Settings > Drips holds the knobs, all settings-table rows per standing rule 12: the master sending switch (same drip_sending_enabled row as the Drips view, so the two mirror each other), the approval gate (drip_approval_required; ON for the launch week, Dylan flips it off for full-auto), and the SMS send window (drip_quiet_start/drip_quiet_end/drip_quiet_days, Arizona time; texts due outside it wait for the next open, emails send any time, and the window also governs blasts). The gate intercepts LIVE campaigns only (dry-run already sends nothing); a leftover pending item keeps its step held even after the gate is switched off, so flipping the gate can never auto-send something a human was reviewing. The Approvals page also hosts the Invoice installments queue (prompt 45; see Deposits and payment schedules).

features.name: Lead detail with AI game plan
features.description: Clicking a lead opens its full page: contact info, an Outreach line (times contacted broken down by calls/texts/emails/drip messages with the last touch, derived from the outbound comms logs and the drip send ledger), notes, and activity timeline on one side, and an AI read on the other with the Hot/Warm/Cold score badge (also shown beside the name up top with the AI's one-line reason), the single best next step, call talking points, and ready-to-copy text and email drafts. Stage changes, note edits, analysis refresh, and Start estimate (which opens the estimator already tied to the lead) all live on the page, and once OpenPhone is connected calls and transcripts appear in the timeline automatically. A Drip section shows the enrollment (active step / stopped reason) with Stop and Enroll buttons, the messages already sent or held (full body behind expandable rows, with a Review shortcut to Drip Approvals when something is waiting), and the UPCOMING steps with their planned dates, so the card answers what is coming next, not just what already went out. Drip messages also appear in the Activity timeline.

features.name: Customers and jobs records
features.description: The core CRM record set: a searchable customer list with structured residential/commercial fields, lead sources, and tags, and a jobs list and pipeline board where each job opens to a redesigned detail page with a line-items estimate table, change-order boxes, notes, job-card fields, price per square foot, and a sticky save bar. Includes CSV customer import in the DripJobs export shape. Prompt 55: jobs.salesperson (frozen from the estimate on accept) is the single display source for who sold the job; the job header shows it (blank = Unassigned), only an admin can change it inline, and a change mirrors to pec_prod_jobs.sales_team over the deal-id bridge and lands in the job activity log.

features.name: Unified Messages inbox
features.description: A Messages tab that merges texts and call logs into one conversation per phone number, newest first, with All/Texts/Calls filters. Every conversation is clickable and replyable, even unknown numbers, which can be attached to a customer (filing all their texts and calls) or turned into a new lead with the phone prefilled. Prompt 38: customer phone numbers render with tap-to-call plus a Text action on the job detail header (routes to that job's comms tab), the lead card and lead detail, the appointment popup, and the printed crew work order; the Text action opens the existing Messages thread (openMessageThread now seeds an empty thread for a number with no history), so consent/STOP and logging stay in this one surface.

features.name: Messages & Calls on the job
features.description: Every job and customer profile has a phone-app-style feed showing the customer's texts and phone calls together in time order, with chat bubbles, call cards, AI call summaries, and full transcripts. Staff text the customer right from the job, and the same feed powers invoice and estimate conversations.

features.name: Job Schedule calendar
features.description: A rolling Week / 3-week production calendar with continuous multi-day job bars, color coded by system, per-week prorated revenue that opens a click-through breakdown, and short per-segment notes (like flake portion) on the bars. Jobs carry their system automatically from the accepted estimate, days are numbered chronologically, and the pending-jobs panel offers quick read-only job details and sizes itself to the calendar. It reflows into a tappable day list on phones. The +Schedule modal also shows the job's CompanyCam site photos read-only (reads jobs.companycam_project_id via the dripjobs_deal_id bridge through the pec-companycam proxy), and both month day pickers ring today's date. Prompt 51: the left aside is now a column holding the Touch-ups panel (see 'Touch-up list and callback tracking') above Pending Jobs, and BOTH pending sources exclude is_callback rows, so an unscheduled touch-up never renders as an ordinary pending job card. The week-revenue exclusion now tests revenue, not the flag: a billable callback (revenue > 0) prorates like any job. Prompt 54: crews themselves stay pec_prod_crews (a crew is a grouping, not a person); people are assigned to crews from Settings > People, writing pec_prod_crew_members.crew_id. Prompt 55: the schedule surfaces (modal, Pending cards, read-only popup, calendar bars, Next Day board + run sheet) autofill system type and estimated hours from the ESTIMATE via one shared helper (prodJobEstimateFacts, backed by buildProdEstimateFacts, the extracted loadCostingData estimate phase), so they always match the Budget card and Job Costing. System: a real pec_prod_areas system (an explicit modal pick) wins; else the estimate-derived system follows live. Hours: a typed override (pec_prod_jobs.estimated_hours) wins on schedule surfaces only; else the computed budgetedHours; costing/bonus keep using the computed number per prompt 50. The modal writes estimated_hours only when the field differs from its prefill, and shows an 'Estimate now says N hrs' drift line with one-click adoption.

features.name: Touch-up list and callback tracking
features.description: A Touch-ups panel in the Job Schedule aside (above Pending Jobs) that tracks every touch-up / warranty callback from request to close. A touch-up stays a full callback job (pec_prod_jobs, is_callback + original_job_id); the panel adds a lifecycle (touchup_state: open / scheduled / waiting_customer / done, a parallel axis to status, which callbacks keep at 'unscheduled'), an age clock (touchup_opened_at; rows go red past touchup_aging_days), manual drag order (touchup_order) with an optional deterministic Sort by suggested (+40 active customer job, +25 crew in the same city in the visible window, +days open capped at 30, -15 waiting; Undo restores touchup_order_prev), and a close flow that REQUIRES a cause from a six-value enum ('other' requires a note) and never deletes anything. Intake is office-only from two places: the panel's + Touch-up (search past jobs by name/address, description + touchup_requested_by) and the job detail toolbar's + Touch-up (prod row resolved by deal id then jobNameAddrKey); both flow through addTouchupCallback (the legacy #schedAddCallback button keeps its confirm + straight-to-scheduler path). Text opens the original job's comms tab with a prefilled draft (one-shot window.__pecCommsPrefill). Billable override: touchup_billable + revenue save together from the schedule modal; the four revenue-exclusion sites test revenue (a null-revenue callback stays $0). The panel's Report modal totals closed touch-ups by cause and by the ORIGINAL job's crew (90 days / YTD) with a callback rate. Callback costs roll up read-only into the parent's unified costing GP display without touching computeCrewBonus inputs (prompt 50's review gate stays the only bonus lever).

features.name: Reschedule / pending flow
features.description: When a job or part of one gets bumped, staff pull specific days off the calendar and the job parks in the Pending column with an amber reschedule badge showing days owed and the date pulled, keeping crew, hours, and price intact until it is rebooked. Calendar tasks, holidays, and days off slot alongside jobs. Clicking a pending job's name or card opens the read-only quick look.

features.name: Next Day Schedule and run sheet
features.description: A focused next-working-day view that lays out each crew's jobs for tomorrow with prorated revenue, plus a Print run sheet button that produces a paper crew sheet. A big job can be split across two crews so it appears under both crew columns in the same slot with a 2 teams badge and on the printed sheet, while staying one job for revenue and status. It stacks into full-width mobile cards. Clicking a job's name on a run-sheet card opens the read-only quick look; dragging the card still moves it between crews and slots. Prompt 51: scheduled touch-ups appear in the crew's column badged TOUCHUP (sky blue, the calendar's callback color) with their description, and print on the run sheet with a plain-text ' - TOUCHUP' marker plus the description line; revenue stays $0 unless the touch-up is billable. The day-revenue total excludes only NO-revenue callbacks.

features.name: Material ordering
features.description: An Ordering view that computes what to buy for scheduled jobs directly from each job card's system and color picks, organized by material (bulk by product plus a by-customer putaway list) with per-line and per-supplier cost. It gates ordering behind a colors-confirmed check so unspecified jobs are not ordered prematurely.

features.name: Price & Material Catalog
features.description: The single catalog of products, materials, flake colors, add-ons, and system-type recipes with pricing that feeds estimating, ordering, and costing. Products carry an explicit cost basis (per gallon/box/pack versus per kit, auto-converted by kit size), each flake carries its own default basecoat, systems show a collapsible one-line recipe summary, and material categories include liquids, flake, quartz, and Polycoat. Admins tune per-system target gross profit and the sundries rate here. Prompt 53: each product can carry two uploaded PDFs, a data sheet (TDS) and an MSDS/SDS, stored as object paths in the public pec-datasheets Supabase Storage bucket (the app's first Storage feature); the list shows TDS/SDS chips and the editor uploads on file pick under a random UUID name so an unsaved product can carry a file.

features.name: Product data sheets (TDS / MSDS)
features.description: Two PDFs per catalog product, a technical data sheet (TDS) and an MSDS/SDS, uploaded from the product editor into the PUBLIC pec-datasheets Supabase Storage bucket (public by decision: crews have no login, and a public URL survives being printed or texted). Rows store the storage object PATH, never a URL; the browser builds links with getPublicUrl. Uploads happen on file pick (object named crypto.randomUUID() + '.pdf'), Save persists the paths, and replaced/removed objects are deleted only after a successful save so a saved row never points at a deleted file. The catalog list shows clickable TDS/SDS chips (dimmed when missing), and the job detail header shows a Data sheets button ONLY when a product in the job's material plan has a sheet, opening a modal of every sheet for the job (material resolution shared with the printed work order via computeJobMaterialLines). Max upload size is the datasheet_max_upload_mb setting (Settings > General); the bucket enforces 10 MB + PDF-only server-side.

features.name: Job costing
features.description: Where a completed job's real costs, materials used, crew hours, and revenue are entered to calculate gross profit, GP/hr, REV/hr, price per square foot (manual job sqft when there are no areas, e.g. custom jobs), and the crew bonus pool. It derives materials from the job card when production lines are empty, supports ad-hoc material lines and editable revenue, and includes a live search across active and completed costings. Prompt 50: the unified detail is an accordion (always-visible profit summary card, collapsible Revenue & Job Info / Labor & Bonus Payout / Materials / Subcontractors / Crew Bonuses / Costs / Notes sections, session-remembered via _unifiedSecOpen, layout only), and the Notes section carries an Office notes box (office_notes/_by/_at on pec_prod_job_costing, saved via saveOfficeNotes with an author+time stamp, separate from the crew-adjacent notes column). openCostingDetail is the superseded modal with no remaining callers. Prompt 51: a parent job's unified detail folds every child touch-up's totalVar into its displayed Total Var and GP via a read-only Callback costs line in the Costs section (clickable through to each touch-up's own costing). Display-layer only: computeCostingRow is untouched, so aggregateCostingRows / Metrics sums count each job's costs once and never double count. Prompt 52: actual crew hours come from the imported BusyBusy Payroll Export rows (wage_type OT1 rows are the OT slice; rows with an unmapped or ignored name never count); a job with imported rows uses them and shows its manual hours greyed for reference, and a finalized job whose live hours drift from the recorded hours_actual snapshot shows a display-only 'Hours changed since finalize' note (the import never writes to bonus tables).

features.name: Costing submit-for-review approval
features.description: Non-admin office staff submit a finished costing for review, which locks the numbers, and an admin finalizes it from a Submitted-for-review queue. Admins can send a costing back with a required reason that reaches the submitter three ways (a banner on the job, a bell notification, and a Slack message) and is kept as a history, and finalizing opens a per-member bonus approval step showing each crew member's suggested bonus for adjustment before it is recorded with a full audit trail.

features.name: Crew bonus and Bonus Report
features.description: Crew bonuses are computed from the labor budget minus actual loaded labor using per-member wages set in Settings, recorded to a ledger on finalize, and tracked as paid or pending in a Bonus Report. Branded one-page print/PDF payout handout sheets can be generated per crew member. Prompt 50 Part E: a bonus becomes payable only bonus_lock_days (default 14) days after the job's completion date on public.jobs.completed_date, bridged from pec_prod_jobs by dripjobs_deal_id then name+address (jobNameAddrKey); a missing completion date reads as LOCKED with a Set completion date affordance, never unlocked. A callback (is_callback + original_job_id) flags the parent job's bonuses for manual review (Pay full / Reduce / Void with review_status/reviewed_by/reviewed_at/review_note; unreviewed = not payable). Paid payouts can be Reversed (admin-only, matching the bp_write is_admin_role() policy): reversed_at/_by/_reason mark the row, it stops counting as paid in every sum and on handouts, and nothing is ever deleted. Prompt 51: the callback cost rollup on the parent's costing is GP display only and does NOT change computeCrewBonus inputs, so the bonus pool on a parent with callbacks is numerically unchanged; the prompt-50 review gate stays the single lever on bonus. Prompt 52: actual hours now come from the BusyBusy Payroll Export import (BusyBusy wins over manual entry when a job has imported rows); OT is BusyBusy's weekly-40 attribution accepted deliberately (the premium lands on whatever job the person was on at hour 40, Dylan's documented tradeoff), and the import never writes to pec_prod_job_bonuses or pec_bonus_payouts. Prompt 54: pec_prod_crew_members rows (ids and hourly_wage) are unchanged and remain the wage source, but they are now mirrored from public.people; wages are editable from Settings > People as well as the legacy Team Members card, both writing the same rows.

features.name: Commission tracking
features.description: A Commission view showing per-salesperson commission as a rate-derived cost baked into the price, with payouts driven off the payment-received date on a Sunday-Saturday period with a Friday payroll check date. Owner-sold jobs are excluded via a per-seller flag, each commission clicks through to its job, and results filter by date range and salesperson. Prompt 54: rates still come from pec_sales_team_members, but pctByName and the exclusion set now also resolve name_aliases (former names captured automatically on any rename by a trigger on pec_sales_team_members), so renaming a rep in the People directory or anywhere else can never silently detach historical pec_job_ar salesperson strings from their rate or exclusion.

features.name: Invoicing and accounts receivable
features.description: An Invoicing module tracking invoices and AR with completed, pending, and cancelled sections, a last-invoiced column, total AR that excludes archived and deposit-in-progress jobs, and a per-invoice Communication history listing every invoice email and text with time, recipient, subject, delivery status, and sender. Supports deposit waivers, recording payments as deposits, and downloadable invoice PDFs. Prompt 38: the Email invoice / Text invoice buttons merged into one split Send control (primary = email + text with the compose modal and text confirm both shown before anything sends; caret = one channel; missing channels send what is on file with a skipped note). Same send code underneath: kind='invoice' SMS with the pay link + STOP line, the compose modal, and the invoice_first_sent_at first-send stamp on either channel. Prompt 40: manual completion is the source of truth. Completed AR rows that were AUTO-completed (jobs.status_manual_at null) but still have a schedule day after today are parked in a 'Completed, but still on the schedule' section and excluded from Total AR; a 'Ready to invoice' section lists in_progress jobs whose last scheduled day has passed, each with a Mark Complete button (markJobComplete, which now also stamps status_manual_at). Schedule spans reach AR rows via the dripjobs_deal_id bridge with the normalized name+address fallback, all reads batched. Prompt 45: the job invoice gains a Payment schedule card (Due-now stat, schedule editor, Prepare deposit), and the send flow is extracted into pecInvoiceSendKit so the Approvals view sends held installments through the identical path.

features.name: Deposits and payment schedules
features.description: Partial invoicing on the one-invoice-per-job model (prompt 45). Accepting an estimate prepares an unsent deposit installment at the resolved default (per-job deposit amount, else the system type's deposit_pct, else the settings default_deposit_pct); staff send it manually. Each invoice can carry a schedule of installments, entered as dollars or a percent of the total (both stored, dollars snapshotted), due on job milestones (acceptance / job start / completion; manual and date exist in schema). Exactly one installment is ever the current ask; the shared resolver in _pec-installments.cjs is the single definition used by the pay page, Stripe, the reminder drip, and the staff UI (client mirror pecInstallmentAsk). Milestone-fired installments queue into an approval hold on the drip runner tick (auto-send via Quo/Resend when the gate is off and the master switch is on); approving sends through the normal invoice send kit with a paid/voided/out-of-turn re-check. The pay page shows the current amount due plus the whole plan, kind=installment charges exactly the server-computed current ask, the webhook settles covered installments, and reminders reference the current ask. A job with no installments behaves exactly as before.

features.name: Metrics and analytics
features.description: A Metrics dashboard of DripJobs-style KPI cards where every metric is drillable to the jobs behind it, filtered by time window and salesperson. Prompt 50: the window control is four presets (MTD default via the metrics_default_window setting, YTD, Last 4 weeks = rolling 28 days, Custom with native date inputs); metricsWindowRange/metricsBuildBuckets drive the WHOLE tab (KPIs, deltas vs an equal-length prior period, charts, Sales section, drip/blast cards, drills), routing around invBuildWeeks; the 12-week preset folded into Custom. A manual-generate AI insights panel at the top writes a plain-language read of the computed values for the selected window (pec-metrics-ai.cjs mode:'tab', cache keyed by window+salesperson in the metrics_tab_ai_insights settings row, TTL from metrics_ai_cache_days), distinct from the weekly pipeline read which stays. Main weekly charts render as Chart.js (lazy CDN, pinned, CSS-bar fallback) with theme-aware ink; speed-to-lead and price-per-sqft draw as gradient-area trend lines, conversion by source gets a rate bar chart, and the Sales volume / Revenue collected / Jobs completed cards carry SVG sparklines. Includes AR-timing KPIs and a Sales section: price per square foot by month and system, speed to lead, conversion by source and campaign, an Outbound touches card, the open pipeline with the AI weekly read, and the Phase 3 drip/blast performance cards.

features.name: Change orders
features.description: Staff add a change order to a job with a system and square footage so pricing suggests itself like the estimator (or a simple title-and-amount mode), and materials and labor flow into job costing. An Additional coat mode adds an extra coat (MVB today, extensible ADDITIONAL_COATS list) to a chosen existing area at its square footage, with an editable price down to $0 for cost-only absorption; the coat rides the area machinery so its product reaches the material pull and costing automatically. The customer signs online, and when a job has two or more unsigned change orders they can be bundled into one approval link and page where a single signature approves them all, with a live link that picks up any change order added later.

features.name: Subcontractor expenses
features.description: An itemized subcontractor card on job costing records who was paid what on subbed-out work, flowing into the job's costs and profit. A whole job can be flagged as subcontracted so hours expectations and crew bonus math skip it.

features.name: Personal to-dos
features.description: A private per-user checklist in the left menu where each person adds items, checks them off, and deletes them. Lists are completely private (not even admins can see them) and sync across every device the user signs in from.

features.name: Admin Ops Queue
features.description: Admin-only Ops Queue view (Overview nav group): one screen of everything stalled or incomplete, so the admin side runs without being told where to look. Ten DERIVED checks computed at render time from live data (unmapped BusyBusy names; costings submitted-not-finalized, read from pec_prod_jobs.costing_submitted_at/costing_finalized_at; scheduled/in-progress/completed jobs with no revenue, callbacks exempt; completed jobs never invoiced; jobs with no salesperson; jobs with no system via the prompt-55 shared estimate helper; drips held for approval; touch-ups open past a threshold; deposits uncollected past a threshold; system health = the schema-drift probe plus open pec_sync_stuck_reports), each row deep-linking to the screen that fixes it, each check toggleable with day thresholds in Settings > General under Ops Queue. Manual items (title, note, assignee from admin_users, due date, Done) and per-record dismissals of derived rows live in pec_ops_items, the only storage; a dismissal is an 'auto' row keyed by check_key (partial unique) so one job's dismissal never hides another's, and derived rows have no Done, they disappear when the data is fixed. Nav badge = open manual items, ONE head-count query at boot (derived checks are page-load work on the view only). Bell: pec_ops_item_notify (SECURITY DEFINER RPC) writes one pec_notifications row (type ops_item, target_view ops) for NEW MANUAL items only; derived checks never bell. RLS staff-read/admin-write via existing is_admin_staff/is_admin_role; no permission changes. NOT the prompt-49 follow-up queue (sales-side, in Leads). The CRM job detail has an admin '+ Ops Queue' action that prefills the item's deep link.

features.name: Notifications
features.description: A live notification bell in the top bar for events like costing submitted or sent back, payments edited or deleted, customer portal activity, and customer estimate views. Notifications are clickable and route straight to their source (the job's costing view, the invoice, the job card, or the estimate card), respecting each user's access.

features.name: People directory and birthdays
features.description: One person = one record (prompt 54). public.people is the source of truth for a person's IDENTITY (name, preferred name, email, phone, month/day birthday, active) across the three legacy person tables: admin_users (logins), pec_sales_team_members (sales reps), pec_prod_crew_members (crew). Roles are the three nullable pointer columns on people; a role is held iff its pointer is set, so the role flag and the identity map can never disagree. Wage, commission %, exclude_from_commission, and crew assignment deliberately STAY on the legacy tables with their readers; Settings > People edits them there inline. Server-side triggers mirror both ways: people edits write through to the legacy rows (name/active, changed fields only), and legacy inserts/renames (pec-create-staff, the legacy cards) auto-adopt/follow so the old surfaces cannot diverge the model. The mirror is switch-off-able via the people_mirror_enabled setting (real rollback, no deploy). Renames are commission-safe: pec_sales_team_members.name_aliases captures every former name via a trigger on that table, and renderCommission resolves aliases (see Commission tracking). Dedupe across the old tables is HUMAN-CONFIRMED only: auto-merge happened solely on matching auth_user_id in the migration backfill; everything else is a suggestion on the Possible duplicates card with Merge (pec_people_merge RPC) / Keep separate (dismissals in the people_merge_dismissed setting). Birthdays: month/day only, NO year stored and no age shown anywhere, required on new adds, backfill nag (dashboard banner + People tab list) until every active person has one, and a reminder at birthday_reminder_lead_days (default 7) as an admin dashboard banner plus a global bell (daily scheduled pec-birthday-reminders.cjs, type 'birthday', target_view 'people' deep-links admins to Settings > People). In-app only; nothing is emailed or texted.

features.name: Per-user permissions
features.description: Role and per-view access controls managed in Settings, defaulting all-on with an admin super-role, so each staff account only sees the views it should (Job Costing, Bonus Report, Commission, Catalog, and Settings are admin-only). Staff accounts, roles, and access are added and managed in the Settings Users area. Prompt 54: staff identity now also lives on public.people (one record per person across logins, sales, crew); admin_users remains the auth/RLS record and is mirrored from people by triggers, and a new admin_users row (pec-create-staff) is auto-adopted as a person. Settings > People is the unified surface; Users stays the place for logins, roles, permissions, and password resets.

features.name: Grouped navigation rail
features.description: The left menu is organized into flyout groups (Overview, Sales, Leads, Estimates, Drips, Production, Finance, Settings, and a pinned Help) that open a submenu of screens, replacing the long flat list, with a mobile Menu button. Jobs pipeline lives under Production; Settings, Pricing, and Sync Health under Settings; the Drips and Settings groups hide entirely for non-admins. Old bookmarks and links keep working.

features.name: What's New changelog
features.description: A plain-language changelog that surfaces new features in a sign-in popup once, keeps the full history in a Help card, and grounds the help assistant. Each user-facing change ships with an entry describing what it does and how to use it.

features.name: In-app help assistant
features.description: A bottom-right Help chat bubble that answers how-to and where-is questions about the app, grounded in a CRM help document, the SOPs, and the What's New history. It explains features and orients users without performing actions or changing data.

features.name: SOP hub
features.description: A standard-operating-procedure hub with an AI SOP chat backend for company processes and documentation. It is kept out of the owner-facing front end but remains available in the codebase.

features.name: Cockpit and JARVIS
features.description: A separate Cockpit workspace reached from the sidebar's Daily flow card, with Dashboard, Execution, and JARVIS tabs. JARVIS is an AI strategy assistant, and the Dashboard gives a quick read on the current state of the business including booked sales.

features.name: Claude-facing MCP server
features.description: A Model Context Protocol server exposing read-only tools (sales summary, customers, jobs, schedule, pipeline) so Claude can answer questions about the business directly against live data.

features.name: Customer portal
features.description: A customer-facing portal, styled to the TopCoat brand, where the customer picks their flake color and signs off, sees an editable per-status project description, and views per-area budget details. Portal activity raises notifications on the internal side.

features.name: Hosted invoice and pay page
features.description: A public, branded invoice page at a private /pay/<token> link where customers view line items and pay online. Redesigned to a premium look with the amount due front and center, it hides pay buttons and shows a PENDING state while a bank transfer clears so no one pays twice. With a payment schedule (prompt 45) the page shows the current amount due as the hero, the full installment plan with paid/upcoming states, and project total/paid/remaining; without one it renders exactly the legacy full-balance page.

features.name: Stripe card and ACH payments
features.description: Online payments through Stripe: customers pay invoices by card or bank transfer (ACH) from the pay link, an internal Charge card option runs a hosted payment for office staff, and payments attach to a named Stripe Customer. ACH settles asynchronously over 3-5 days, recording itself on clearing, showing pending markers, and raising a failure alert and red chip if a transfer bounces. Includes editable and deletable (audited, cascade-guarded) payment records with an activity log. kind=installment (prompt 45) charges exactly the current installment amount computed server-side from the token; the webhook settles covered installments after recording.

features.name: Resend email pipeline
features.description: A transactional email pipeline (Resend) for sending branded invoices and documents with a compose-before-send step, a Settings Email panel, editable templates with a real-view preview, and per-send delivery logging.

features.name: Email log
features.description: A top-level Email Log view (all staff, like Messages) listing every email the system sent from pec_email_log, newest first, with a customer name/address search, type and status filters, a date range, and delivery detail (opens, clicks, bounces from the Resend webhook). Clicking a row opens the full email: transactional sends store their final wrapped HTML in pec_email_log.body_html going forward (rendered in a sandboxed iframe), drip and blast rows read their body from the pec_drip_sends ledger (provider_id = resend_id), and rows that predate body capture show a clear not-captured note. The same rows embed read-only as an Emails card at the bottom of the customer detail and job detail pages. PEC only, no brand filter. Known gaps: internal office alert emails (invoice payment-intent, estimate accept/decline, Stripe ACH-failure) and Supabase auth emails (password resets) do not write pec_email_log.

features.name: Quo / OpenPhone integration
features.description: Integration with the office phone (Quo/OpenPhone) powering two-way SMS from customer profiles and jobs, a Text invoice button that sends the pay link, STOP-based opt-out enforcement, and automatic call logging with AI summaries, next steps, and full transcripts on customer profiles and lead timelines.

features.name: DripJobs integration
features.description: The inbound-deal integration that auto-bridges DripJobs proposals into the CRM via webhooks (proposal accepted, stage changed, project completed), writing jobs to both the Jobs page and the Job Schedule. A DripJobs Sync Health view makes missing, partial, or silently failed ingestion visible so staff can confirm jobs are syncing.

features.name: CompanyCam integration
features.description: Job photos come from CompanyCam via a staff-authenticated proxy, with a searchable project picker on the job detail and a navigable fullscreen photo viewer that zooms and pans (double click, wheel, pinch). The Job Schedule's +Schedule modal shows the same photos read-only.

features.name: BusyBusy hours import (Payroll Export)
features.description: Crew hours reach job costing through an admin-triggered, preview-then-commit import from the BusyBusy Payroll Export API (Settings > BusyBusy). The API is a snapshot, not a sync (calculated Ids, no updatedSince, no deletion feed), so each import atomically replaces the stored date window via the pec_busybusy_import RPC; re-importing after punch corrections is the normal workflow. Identity is name-only (the export's EmployeeId is empty): every exported name is mapped to a crew member or Ignored on the mapping screen, and projects link to jobs once by exact normalized customer name, then by their stable 7-digit ProjectNumber (no fuzzy matching, ever). Overtime is BusyBusy's weekly-40 attribution, stored verbatim as REG/OT1 rows (a punch crossing hour 40 arrives as a split pair sharing Start/End); hours aggregate at read time, and BusyBusy's Wage/Cost columns are deliberately never imported. Overhead projects (Shop) are stored and reported but never charge a job. Anomalies (long punches, overlaps, punch notes) import and are flagged in the preview, never auto-corrected. Manual labor entry remains for jobs with no BusyBusy coverage; a job with imported rows uses them and shows its manual entries greyed. The earlier GraphQL proxy (pec-busybusy.cjs, 401 since 2026-06-13, spec docs/archive/prompts/claude-code-prompt-busybusy-overtime-costing.md) was retired by this build. Prompt 54: crew-member identity (pec_prod_crew_members.id, which pec_prod_busybusy_employees.crew_member_id maps to) is untouched by the People model; the mirror only writes name/active and never rewrites ids, so imported-hour attribution is stable.

features.name: Google Sheets bridge
features.description: The original data bridge using Google Sheets (Booked Jobs and Dashboard Data sheets) via an Apps Script proxy to feed the dashboard's booked-sales and revenue figures, since migrated toward Supabase-native reads.

features.name: Slack notifications
features.description: Outbound Slack alerts to the #epoxysales channel for key sales and production events, including estimate accepted or declined and costings sent back with their reason.

features.name: Revenue goals home
features.description: Owner home screen tracking booked-sales revenue pace plus the annual scorecard, rocks, meeting rhythm, and projects cards, sourced from Google Sheets.

features.name: Owner task list
features.description: Owner personal task list synced through a Google Sheet, separate from crew tasks and the private per-user to-dos.

features.name: Staff authentication
features.description: Supabase email and password sign-in with owner-versus-employee shell gating, password reset, a global auth gate, and sign-in event logging.

features.name: Job activity log
features.description: Per-job audit trail card showing who changed what and when, plus the job status-change modal.

features.name: Admin landing dashboard
features.description: The admin CRM landing view shown after sign-in, giving a quick overview before drilling into specific screens.

features.name: Color catalog admin
features.description: Admin screen for the flake color catalog: add and edit colors that feed the customer portal color picker and material ordering.

features.name: Referrals tracking
features.description: Simple tracking of customer referrals with an add/edit form.

features.name: Reviews
features.description: Read-only view of collected customer reviews.

features.name: Schedule status auto-sync
features.description: Boot-time sweep plus a scheduled daily function that flip job status from scheduled to in progress based on the production schedule, so statuses stay honest without manual edits. The one canonical rule is deriveJobStatus (client) in lockstep with the pec_prod_jobs_sync_public_status trigger (2026-07-21_manual_completion_source_of_truth.sql). Since 2026-07-21 nothing auto-completes: a job past its last scheduled day stays in_progress until a human marks it complete, and only the manual completion paths stamp completed_date.

features.name: Appointments calendar
features.description: A top-level Appointments view (Sales group, all staff): a Month/Week/Day calendar of sales appointments (on-site estimates, project walkthroughs, site visits, and ad-hoc 'other' blocks), separate from the crew Job Schedule. Each appointment is assigned to a pec_sales_team_members roster member (per-member event color, per-type accent, type + salesperson filters with an All Users default). Create from the New Appointment button or a day/slot tap; edit, cancel, delete, drag-to-reschedule and resize. Renders with FullCalendar 6 lazy-loaded from cdnjs and degrades to a month list that still edits when the CDN is blocked. Booking a lead-linked appointment notifies the bell (log_appointment_booked RPC) and kicks pec-appt-notify for the consent-checked customer confirmation; the scheduled pec-appt-reminder-runner sends the configured offset reminders (rules edited in Settings > Appointments). Schedule Estimate on a lead prefills the form and advances a new lead to contacted. Prompt 38: appointment notes are split into customer-facing Job notes (pec_appointments.customer_notes, appended to the customer's confirmation/reminder texts and emails on both channels, scrubbed of em dashes) and internal Company notes (pec_appointments.notes, pushed to the Google event description composed with an auto-added customer name/phone + a /?appt=<id> TopCoat deep link above a '----' separator; the pull ingests only the human-typed part back). The appointment popup also shows the linked lead/customer's phone with tap-to-call and tap-to-text. Prompt 43: booking a lead-linked appointment also pauses the lead's active nurture drip (enrollment stopped with reason appointment_booked) via the shared server helper apptBookingLeadEffects in _pec-appt.cjs, called from the pec-appt-notify on-book kick; appointments can also arrive from Routemize (see the Routemize appointment intake entry).

features.name: Routemize appointment intake
features.description: The webhook path that makes Routemize (prescottepoxycompany.routemize.com) the booking front end and TopCoat's appointment calendar the system of record after DripJobs retirement. Zapier posts every Routemize appointment event (created / updated / canceled / deleted) to pec-appt-intake with the shared webhook secret; the endpoint upserts pec_appointments by routemize_appt_id (source 'routemize', bare datetimes read as America/Phoenix), matches the contact to a live lead by last-10 phone or email (customer fallback; never auto-creates either), and maps the assigned rep to the pec_sales_team_members roster by google_email else name. A Routemize delete marks the row canceled, never hard-deletes, so the existing Google push removes the calendar event on its next kick. A NEW lead-linked booking reproduces the in-app booking's lead-side state through the shared server helper apptBookingLeadEffects (_pec-appt.cjs): a new lead with a booked on-site estimate advances to contacted with a stage_change lead_event, the lead's active nurture drip stops with reason appointment_booked (in-app bookings get the same drip pause via the pec-appt-notify kick), a staff bell row lands, and a best-effort runApptReminders kick sends the consented customer confirmation immediately (the 15-minute runner is the safety net). Every attempt logs to pec_webhook_ingest_log (endpoint 'appt-intake') for the Sync Health view. Unmatched contact or rep never blocks the appointment: it lands unlinked/unassigned with the details noted in the internal Company notes.

features.name: Google Calendar two-way sync
features.description: Per-member Google Calendar sync for the Appointments calendar. Each roster member connects their OWN Google account from Settings > Appointments (OAuth: pec-google-oauth-start mints an HMAC-signed-state consent URL, pec-google-oauth-callback exchanges the code, creates-or-reuses a dedicated 'TopCoat' secondary calendar in their account, and stores tokens in the service-role-only pec_sales_member_google_tokens vault; connection status the UI reads lives as flags on pec_sales_team_members). TopCoat pushes appointment create/update/cancel/delete into that TopCoat calendar (pec-appt-sync-push, kicked fire-and-forget from apptPostWrite), and the scheduled pec-google-calendar-pull polls it every 15 minutes with incremental syncTokens (410 = full resync), upserting by google_event_id with an echo/last-writer-wins rule on google_updated. Personal (primary) calendars are never read or written. Requires GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID/SECRET in Netlify env; everything no-ops cleanly while unconfigured. Prompt 38: the pushed event description = internal Company notes + a separator + an auto-added contact/link block (composeGcalDescription/stripGcalDescription in _pec-google.cjs); the pull strips the auto block so a Google-side description edit only ever lands in notes, and customer_notes never crosses to or from Google.

features.name: Address autocomplete (HQ)
features.description: Google Places address autocomplete on the HQ dashboard, ported from the estimator PWA's places.ts onto vanilla index.html (current AutocompleteSuggestion / Place.fetchFields surface, session-token billing hygiene, silent degrade offline or with no key). Wired into the appointment form's address field (fills city/state/zip + location_place_id) and the New Lead modal (which gained split city/state/zip inputs that now persist to the leads columns). Uses the existing domain-restricted browser key from netlify.toml's secret-scan omit list; suggestions only appear once the Maps JavaScript + Places APIs are enabled on that key in Google Cloud Console. Customer/job forms deliberately not wired this pass.

features.name: Migration drift detection
features.description: Detects repo migrations that were never applied to prod (the failure that let 2026-07-18_crew_notes.sql silently break every estimator save for a week). Every migration dated 2026-07-01+ carries a machine-readable @artifacts header (CLAUDE.md rule 13) declaring the tables/columns/indexes/settings it creates; scripts/build-migration-manifest.mjs compiles the headers into netlify/functions/_migration-manifest.json at build time (wired into netlify.toml's build command), and pec-migration-drift.cjs probes every declared artifact against the LIVE schema in one batched pec_schema_probe RPC call (migration 2026-07-25_migration_drift_probe.sql; read-only SECURITY DEFINER, service-role-only). Artifact probing, not filename matching, because schema_migrations names do not match repo filenames, and it also catches PARTIALLY applied migrations. Runs daily at 07:00 MST plus on demand from Settings > Diagnostics > Schema Drift (four buckets: applied / missing / partial / not-verifiable, plus informational reverse drift = live tables no repo SQL creates). Missing/partial raise de-duped admin bells (never re-notifies while one is unread); reverse drift never notifies. Knobs: migration_drift_check_enabled, migration_drift_baseline.

features.name: Estimator stuck-sync visibility
features.description: Replaces the quiet 'N to sync' counter that hid a week of failing saves. Retry policy (production/outbox-drain.cjs, fixture-tested by production/outbox-backoff.test.cjs): per-op backoff 1m/5m/30m then hourly, deliberately NO maximum-attempts cap (the crew_notes incident self-healed only because ops were still retrying); children of a failed or deferred parent are skipped for the pass, transitively, with attempts untouched, so one root cause reads as one problem. Header shows three states: Online, Online · N to sync, or a RED 'N saves not syncing · oldest X days' once any op reaches sync_stuck_threshold_attempts (default 2, reaches the PWA via catalog.ts settings). The red state expands to per-op detail (attempts, stuck-for, lastError verbatim) with a Retry now that force-clears backoff. Server escalation: once per session the PWA POSTs stuck-op metadata (ids and error only) to pec-sync-stuck.cjs, which upserts pec_sync_stuck_reports on op_id and bells the office once per op; gated by sync_stuck_escalation_enabled. Knobs live in Settings > Estimates.

features.name: Two-factor authentication (2FA)
features.description: Opt-in TOTP two-factor authentication for staff logins. A shield button in the topbar (next to logout, visible to every signed-in staff member) opens an enroll/manage modal: scan a QR into an authenticator app, verify a 6-digit code, and 2FA turns on; it can also be turned back off. Enrolled users are challenged for a code at sign-in (passwordSignIn -> pecMfaLoginChallenge); users without a factor pass straight through, so it is inert until someone opts in. Uses the Supabase GoTrue MFA API (no app tables). Enforcement for everyone (gating on AAL2) is a deliberate later step. Requires TOTP enabled in the Supabase Auth dashboard.

features.name: Security hardening & monitoring
features.description: Server-side authorization and monitoring from the 2026-07-25 security review. requireStaff() (in _pec-supabase.cjs) validates a caller's Supabase JWT AND confirms an admin_users row before any service-role endpoint acts (send-sms/email, blast-run, metrics-ai, estimate-*, lead-ai, drip-approve, appt-notify, sheets-proxy, sync-stuck, sop-chat, log-signin, notify-costing-sendback, migration-drift manual). safeEqual() gives constant-time secret compares. DB-side: log_* notification RPCs guard on is_admin_staff and anon EXECUTE revoked; RLS RBAC via has_permission() on commissions/costing/catalog; audit_log made append-only. pec-security-monitor.cjs (scheduled every 15m) Slacks an alert on a staff sign-in from a never-before-seen IP, gated by security_alerts_enabled.
